title.narrative: Africa Regional Scholarship and Innovation Fund for Applied Sciences, Engineering and Technology

description.narrative: The objective of the Africa Regional Scholarship and Innovation Fund for Applied Sciences, Engineering and Technology Project is to strengthen the institutional capacity for quality and sustainable doctoral training, research and innovation in transformative technologies in sub-Saharan Africa. There are two components to the project, the first component being capacity development for the operation and management of the scholarship, research and innovation fund. This component will support strengthening of the RCU to become a scientific, technological and innovation capacity builder for PhD programs and universities in SSA in the fields of applied sciences and engineering that support transformative technologies, to make it capable of operating and growing RSIF efficiently and sustainably. This component includes four subcomponents: capacity building for managing and growing the RSIF general fund and setting up a RSIF permanent fund, capacity development for the operation and management of doctoral training scholarships in selected African universities and research grants in ASET fields, capacity development for improving quality of PhD programs and research in ASET fields, and capacity development for the operation and management of innovation grants. The second component is the Scholarships and Research Grants for ASET. This component, financed by a US$9 million22 contribution from the Government of Korea administered by the Bank, will provide financing for scholarships and research grants in ASET fields in Sub-Saharan Africa. SSA countries have shown interest in contributing funds to RSIF either through their own resources or through national/regional IDA credit. Some of these contributions may also be channeled through regional IDA projects, for instance the third ACE, which is currently under preparation. This component includes two subcomponents: doctoral training in ASET fields in selected SSA host Universities and international partner universities, and research grants.
To strengthen the institutional capacity for quality doctoral training, research, and innovation in transformative technologies in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

title.narrative: Number of research grants awarded to faculty of RSIF host institutions

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Six Research Awards (Research Grants Type 1) were given to faculty of RSIF Host Universities in 2019. Four of the six projects have completed implementation and been successfully closed. Some have produced prototypes from their research work, e.g., the University of Rwanda's project on indoor air pollution and the Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology's project on a solar-heated pump dryer. The projects have cumulatively contributed to a total of 50 publications. An additional 10 Research Award projects, awarded to faculty of RSIF AHUs in November 2021, are progressing well in developing prototypes, disseminating research, and improving research infrastructure at the AHUs. Of the 10, four have completed implementation and have been closed out.

title.narrative: Number of research grants awarded to faculty of RSIF host institutions

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Sixteen Research Awards (Research Grant Type 1) were awarded to faculty of RSIF Host Universities — six in the first round (2020) and ten in the second round (2021). All projects completed implementation and developed prototypes, contributed to publications, and strengthened research infrastructure at the AHUs. Collectively, the research projects have produced 55 publications in reputable journals, two policy briefs and 12 technologies.

title.narrative: Number of research grants awarded to RSIF scholars

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. Ten RSIF PhD graduates who have returned to their home institutions were competitively awarded Junior Investigator Research Awards (JIRA) of up to US$80,000 each for research activities conducted in collaboration with international partners. With funding from the Carnegie Corporation of New York under the DOCTAS project, the RCU awarded five grants of US$50,000 to RSIF graduates in August 2024 and an additional eight JIRA grants in April 2025, bringing the total number of JIRA grants awarded to 23. So far, the JIRA projects have started to produce outputs, including publications, 12 prototypes, and participation in short trainings to build complementary skills. Out of the 23 grants, six have completed implementation, and the remaining 17 are in progress.

title.narrative: Number of research papers submitted by staff members or scholars supported by the project for publication to internationally indexed journals

comment.narrative: End target exceeded. A total of 427 high-quality peer-reviewed scientific papers have been published by staff members/faculty, scholars, and grantees, 138 of which were authored by women. Of the 427 publications, 392 are by scholars and 69 by grantees (34 co-authored by scholars in funded research projects, and 6 from the AGriDI project). Cohort 1 has published 63 peer-reviewed and conference papers, while Cohorts 2, 3, and 4 have published 146, 106, and 74 papers, respectively. In addition, 1 paper is co-authored by Cohort 1 and Cohort 3 scholars, and 2 papers are co-authored by Cohort 3 and Cohort 4 scholars. The 427 total publications have been cited 3,826 times (self-citations excluded), with 529,375 full-text downloads and 509,324 abstract views, and an impact factor range of 0–19.3. icipe continues to support RSIF scholars and faculty at AHUs in writing high-quality articles and publishing them in relevant international journals.

title.narrative: Number of innovation grants awarded to faculty of RSIF host institutions

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Five Cooperability Grants (Innovation Grant Type 2)—two awarded in October 2020 and three in November 2021—all completed implementation by October 2025 and produced minimum viable products. For example, the Smart Bee Hiving Technology project awarded to the University of Rwanda developed and tested a prototype that was piloted in the market, and some farmers have adopted the technology and reported increased honey productivity. The Biopesticide project awarded to UFHB developed two biopesticides, which were approved and registered by the Ministry of Agriculture, Côte d’Ivoire. The university also established a production facility to scale up.

title.narrative: Number of innovation grants awarded to faculty of RSIF host institutions

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Two Cooperability Grants (Innovation Grants Type 2), which require collaboration with the private sector, commenced implementation in October 2020 and have so far produced prototypes of their products. An additional three Cooperability Grants (Innovation Grants Type 2), awarded to faculty of the University of Rwanda, Kenyatta University, and the African University of Science & Technology in November 2021, are under implementation. The two projects awarded in the first round in 2020 have been completed: the Smart Bee Hiving Technology project, awarded to the University of Rwanda, developed and tested a prototype that has been piloted in the market; and the Biopesticide project, awarded to UFHB, developed two biopesticides that were approved and registered by the Ministry of Agriculture, Côte d’Ivoire. The RCU has successfully closed out these two completed projects. The other three projects awarded in 2021 are in the process of closure and are preparing final reports.

title.narrative: Number of innovation grants awarded to RSIF host universities

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Six (6) Institutional Innovation Capacity Building Grants (Innovation Type 1) were awarded in November 2020. title.narrative: Number of RSIF scholars who graduate PhD programs

comment.narrative: On track. There are a total of 67 scholars who have graduated from RSIF PhD programs. title.narrative: Number of RSIF scholars who graduate PhD programs

comment.narrative: Target substantially achieved (91.5%). There are a total of 75 scholars who have graduated from RSIF PhD programs. title.narrative: Number of RSIF host institutions that start the international accreditation process at the PhD program level or at the institution level

comment.narrative: On track. During the restructuring in December 2021, the indicator was adjusted to measure the “start” of the international accreditation process, which implies that the RSIF institution has identified an international accreditation agency, signed a contract with the agency, and completed self-evaluation for the accreditation process. Accordingly, the RCU conducted an assessment of the accreditation of the target programs at AHUs and supported the AHUs in initiating the required accreditation. The required support for accreditation is incorporated into the overall capacity-building strategy for AHUs. So far, eight (8) AHUs have either started or completed the accreditation process with support from the ACE Impact projects. There are two additional AHUs that have started self-assessment as an initial step in the accreditation process. With additional financial support, KU and UoN would be able to complete the self-assessment process, and the target would be met by December 2025.

title.narrative: Percentage of RSIF scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2 employed/self-employed in their field of study at least 6 months after graduation (% of female graduates employed/self-employed).

comment.narrative: End target exceeded. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021, which reflects the percentage of students who have graduated and obtained employment six months after graduation compared to the total number of potential graduates in Cohorts 1 and 2. Of the 15 Cohort 1 scholars (3 female), 11 (2 female) completed their studies, and all 11 (2 female) are employed. Of the 61 Cohort 2 scholars (27 female), 44 (18 female) had completed their studies as of September 2025, and 34 (13 female) of them are employed as postdoctoral fellows, faculty members, or researchers in various institutions. In summary, 45 out of 55 Cohort 1 and 2 graduates are employed, which makes up 81 percent. The employment rate for female scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2 is also 75 percent (i.e., 15 out of 20 graduated female scholars).

title.narrative: Level of satisfaction of RSIF Scholars with the quality of the learning environment and delivery of the target doctoral programs at the AHUs.

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The level of satisfaction among RSIF scholars is assessed based on the quality of the doctoral content, curriculum/training delivery, faculty/staff, and teaching and learning facilities. This figure was derived from the 2024 RSIF student satisfaction survey. It is based on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = Very Unsatisfied, 2 = Unsatisfied, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Satisfied, 5 = Very Satisfied). The indicator reflects the percentage of enrolled students who rated their satisfaction at levels 4 or 5 on the Likert scale.

title.narrative: Level of satisfaction of RSIF Scholars with the quality of the learning environment and delivery of the target doctoral programs at the AHUs.

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The level of satisfaction among RSIF scholars was assessed based on the quality of the doctoral content, curriculum/training delivery, faculty/staff, and teaching and learning facilities. This figure was derived from the 2025 RSIF student satisfaction survey and is based on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = Very Unsatisfied, 2 = Unsatisfied, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Satisfied, 5 = Very Satisfied). The indicator captures the percentage of enrolled students who rated their satisfaction at levels 4 or 5 on the Likert scale. Overall satisfaction increased from 85% in 2024 to 86.5% in 2025, reflecting improvements in IPI matching, access to academic resources and infrastructure, and awareness and satisfaction with GRM processes.

title.narrative: Percentage of RSIF scholars in Cohorts 1 and 2 employed/self-employed in their field of study at least 6 months after graduation (% of female graduates employed/self-employed).

comment.narrative: End target exceeded. This indicator, introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021, reflects the percentage of students who have graduated and obtained employment six months after graduation compared to the total number of potential graduates in Cohorts 1 and 2. Of the 15 Cohort 1 scholars (3 female), 11 (2 female) completed their studies, and all 11 are employed. Of the 61 Cohort 2 scholars (27 female), 45 (18 female) had completed their studies as of September 2025, and 41 (16 female) were employed as postdoctoral fellows, faculty members, researchers, consultants, or entrepreneurs. In total, 52 out of 56 Cohort 1 and 2 graduates are employed, representing 93 percent. The employment rate for female scholars in these cohorts is 90 percent (i.e., 18 out of 20 graduated female scholars).

title.narrative: Set up a foundation for establishment of the permanent fund.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The definition of the indicator for establishing the foundation of the permanent fund included a set of core documents—feasibility study, financial model, implementation plan, funding strategy, investment policy, and fund manager TORs—all of which were completed. Ideas for an RSIF permanent fund by Ai2 Advisory—Carbon X Green and a Venture Capital Fund—were presented to the PASET CAG and EB on February 1, 2023, in Kigali, Rwanda, and were assessed as requiring further analysis. The Fulbright specialist project in 2024 revived the concept of a restricted permanent fund based on icipe's 501(c)(3) status, which was presented to PASET together with an updated RSIF case for support. icipe plans to establish the restricted permanent fund as part of its integrated capacity development platform under icipe's 2026–2030 vision and strategy, launched on 21 November 2025.

title.narrative: Set up a foundation for establishment of the permanent fund.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. This is a new indicator introduced during the project restructuring in December 2021. The definition of the indicator for the foundation of the establishment of the permanent fund included a comprehensive feasibility study, a financial model, an implementation plan, a funding strategy, a draft board charter, an investment policy, and fund manager TORs. These documents have been completed, and an Advisory Committee was proposed. Ideas for RSIF permanent fund by Ai2 Advisory—Carbon X Green and a Venture Capital Fund—were presented to the PASET CAG and EB on February 01, 2023, in Kigali, Rwanda, and were deemed to require further study on the viability of carbon financing. In collaboration with the PASET structures, icipe is exploring financial models, and the 6th PASET Forum with a focus on resource mobilization was held on April 23–25, 2024, in Nairobi, Kenya, and a Governing Council meeting will be held on September 26–28, 2025.
